A1.justification: Both PDFs address prediction instability caused by VLM acceleration and carry the same arXiv identity, despite substantial reframing. All 10 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v3 are readable, including v3 Appendices A–G; v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original LoFi evaluations, computational costs, LID–consistency correlations, and pruning ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of token reduction and quantization, input perturbation experiments, medical evaluations, and cross-method divergence analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v1 proposes LoFi: SVD-derived token leverage scores, IPR-dependent dynamic pruning, and weighted merging of removed tokens. This entire acceleration method is removed in v3, which evaluates existing acceleration techniques without proposing a replacement acceleration algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 retains GQA, VQAv2, and TextVQA and adds AI2D, ScienceQA, OKVQA, VizWiz, MMBench, MMMU, and POPE. It also evaluates biomedical conversations and VQA-RAD, extending coverage to medical imaging and questions. Visual and textual perturbations introduce additional input conditions absent from v1.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain VisionZip but remove PruMerge+ and TRIM, including their finetuned variants. v3 adds PyramidDrop, SparseVLM, FastV, and HiRED to the token-reduction comparisons and evaluates AWQ, GPTQ, and LLM.int8() against unaccelerated models. These are actual evaluated methods in Tables 1–2 and Appendix E.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates accuracy, intended output agreement, and TFLOPs across pruning budgets. v3 reports performance drops, DR, and newly introduced NDR, with additional F1 and medical recall evaluations; TFLOP reporting disappears. It adds quantization configurations and controlled perturbation procedures. VisionZip's 192/128/64-token sweep becomes a single 192-token setting, while Qwen and medical model configurations expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v1's LID–consistency analysis and dynamic-versus-fixed pruning ablation are removed. v3 adds visual/textual robustness experiments, analysis of overlap between negatively diverged instances across methods in Appendix D, and qualitative divergence examples across general and medical models in Appendix G.

E5.justification: v1's explicit Pearson-correlation estimation between LID and consistency is removed with Section 5.2 and Table 2. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's distribution plots display benchmark results rather than uncertainty across repeated runs.

E6.justification: LoFi performance, TFLOPs, LID correlations, and pruning-ablation results disappear, while extensive DR/NDR, perturbation, and medical results are added. For example, v3 Table 2 reports average DR 20.72% and NDR 6.55% for GPTQ on LLaVA-1.5. Shared benchmark values also change: baseline LLaVA-1.5 VQAv2 accuracy is 78.53% in v1 versus 76.64% in v3. Incompletely matched settings preclude interpreting these differences as direct performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v1's mathematical development of LID and LoFi, including the IPR aggregation, leverage scores, dynamic pruning rule, and weighted merging in Equations 1–12, is removed. v3 explicitly defines DR and the additional correct-to-incorrect NDR category. v1's consistency prose describes agreement although its displayed formula counts disagreement; v3's DR definition makes disagreement explicit. No theorem or proof replaces the removed mathematical development.

C1.justification: v1 claims contributions in explaining internal disruption and mitigating it through LoFi. v3 drops both contributions and positions the paper as a large-scale empirical investigation of VLM acceleration instability. The retained claim that aggregate performance masks prediction changes expands to quantization, perturbed inputs, and medical applications.

C2.justification: v1's explanations connecting internal energy distributions, layer redundancy, and consistency preservation are removed. v3 introduces interpretations concerning harmful prediction flips, deployment under noisy inputs, medical risks, and limited cross-method overlap complicating mitigation. Its new limitations section explicitly cautions that academic benchmarks and simulated perturbations may not generalize quantitatively to industrial environments.

D1.justification: v3 Appendices A–C substantially expand reproducibility information with dataset splits and sample counts, accelerator hyperparameters, perturbation catalogs and severity levels, and reuse of identical perturbed inputs across methods. It specifies a default 7B model size, with a 3B Qwen2-VL exception in Appendix E. Splits for retained benchmarks are newly documented, not established as changed. LoFi-specific settings disappear with the method.

R1.justification: Related work expands from VLMs and token pruning to quantization and compression evaluation. v3 discusses Dutta et al.'s instance-level flip metric, LLMCBench, and Wen et al.'s critique of token-pruning evaluation, among other additions. References underpinning LoFi's SVD/IPR approach disappear, and novelty is repositioned around empirical evaluation of VLM acceleration stability.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, results narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method-centered structure is replaced by experimental settings followed by standard-benchmark, perturbation, and medical investigations, with a new limitations section and Appendices A–G. This is substantial narrative reconstruction beyond accommodating additional results.

P2.justification: The LoFi framework diagram, LID correlation plot, and original result-table structures are removed. v3 introduces broad benchmark matrices with highlighted NDR values, perturbation tables, medical tables, distribution plots, an overlap heatmap, and numerous qualitative example panels. Figure 1 is redrawn around a medical example, and the document's table and figure layout is extensively reorganized.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the shared instability investigation through harmful-flip measurement, broader evaluations, and better settings and limitations documentation, while relinquishing v1's mechanistic and mitigation contributions. However, new reporting inconsistencies undermine confidence: Table 2 gives LLaVA-Next/GPTQ on OKVQA DR 1.51% but NDR 5.25%, conflicting with NDR's stated relationship to DR. Table 11 also labels the FastV GQA drop as 0.018% versus 1.83% in Table 1, and Appendix F interprets such scales as exceptionally small losses. These benefits and reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
